summary.text:
Vakyartha (`vak`) is a local-first agent harness for one owner: agents that work on code, documents, research and everyday tasks, reached from a desktop app, the browser, a terminal and chat apps, with every model input and tool result kept in an append-only record. Its thesis is strong safety, transparent operation, extensible integrations and a simple core.

The lower layers (storage, permission, the pure deciders, the document engines) are well shaped and change rarely. Above them, three large crates (`vak-core`, `vak-agent`, `vak-server`) hold the turn and most features, and that is where most of the work and most of the risk sit.

unreleased: Route planning stops on unreadable evidence instead of planning from an incomplete history.
Budget reservations retain unresolved costs when recording fails and keep their original attribution.
Live outcome revisions and steering messages must be recorded before they change the running contract or reach the model.
Two dependency updates clear seven known vulnerabilities:
Concurrent credential updates preserve every presence marker, and trust checks treat unreadable presence metadata conservatively.
Commitment admission and portfolio reads report unreadable history instead of treating it as an empty portfolio.
Chart category labels retain their original text, including leading zeroes and punctuation.
Charts retain tiny ranges, distinguish nearby values and position extreme finite values without overflowing.
Tools stop before execution if their assistant message cannot be saved.
Saved answer and page views reopen in the Canvas after a reload.
Calls whose effects are unknown wait for other potentially mutating calls instead of bypassing resource conflict checks.
Artifact changes stop before deciding or writing when their history is unreadable.
Search, lists and tool-history queries refresh sharing permissions before returning results, and report unreadable sharing records instead of trusting stale grants.
Stopping a recovery probe no longer leaves a provider permanently unavailable.
Grant-service permission checks, outbound-action decisions and connected account reads now fail when new records cannot be read, rather than silently trusting cached state.
Ref writes and removals check the current writer epoch atomically with their commit record, so a restored store refuses a stale writer even when the two operations race.

findings.title: A turn's decisions share mutable state inside two outlier functions
findings.evidence: Clippy's `cognitive_complexity` scores `Agent::run_message_inner` at 194 (rank 1 of 4,348 library functions) and `Core::run_turn_recorded` at 103 (rank 3); the median is 3 and the 99th percentile 24. 148 commits changed the first (6% of all) and 207 the second (9%). Fix commits land in `vak-core/src/lib.rs` at 10.2 and `vak-agent/src/lib.rs` at 9.2 per thousand lines, against a median of 4.5 over 396 files; file size alone does not predict the rate (ρ = -0.14).
findings.matters: The loop keeps the turn's decisions in mutable locals that every step and every call result updates. `948ece43d` fixed two bugs of exactly that kind: `receipts.unresolved_error` was cleared by a later success in the same batch even when an earlier call had failed, and `verification_stale` came out stale or not depending on which parallel result returned first. Both were fixed by moving the decision into a pure function over the whole batch, tested on its own.
findings.fix: Do that for the rest: the turn's state as one type, each decision a pure function of it, and the end-of-turn checks (among them goal mode's audit, the managed-work gate and the commitment hold, which judge durable work at different scopes on purpose) as one ordered list with tests of how they combine. Context planning and the model call can stay as they are.

findings.title: The rule that wrappers forward every Tool declaration is enforced by nothing
findings.evidence:
The trait's width is deliberate: a tool declares what it is (34 methods, 30 with a default) so that nothing decides by a tool's name. AGENTS.md then requires that "a wrapper forwards every declaration", and no test checks it. 2 wrappers forward by hand, and one that forgets compiles cleanly and answers with the default:

- `ScopedWriteTool` (`crates/vak-agent/src/write_lease.rs:142`): does not forward `card_block`, `card_kinds`, `changes_workspace`, `presents_cards`
- `BrokeredTool` (`crates/vak-tools/src/broker.rs:349`): does not forward `card_block`, `card_kinds`, `presents_cards`
findings.matters: `fill_defaults` joined the trait on 2026-10-07 (`fb981ed3d`), and both wrappers began forwarding it only on 2026-10-12 (`53dbc16f8`): for five days every brokered tool lost its argument aliases. The gaps listed above answer correctly today only because no wrapped tool overrides those methods.
findings.fix: A test that fails when a wrapper leaves a defaulted method unforwarded, or a delegation macro that forwards them all.
findings.sources: `crates/vak-tools/src/lib.rs` (`pub trait Tool`); AGENTS.md; `git log -S` per method; `evidence.py` `tool_wrappers`.

findings.title: Storage's guarantees are not tested in the shapes that broke them
findings.evidence: Owning the storage layer is a decision (docs/decisions.md, 2026-10-18), and it is tested for torn writes, crashes, fsync paths and injected faults, with a fuzz corpus. Nothing tests a chain's reader against a simple reference model, and few tests run two writer processes. The two P1 faults of 2026-10-18 needed exactly those shapes: a cached grant that kept authorizing because its revocation sat in an unreadable segment (A01), and a writer paused between the epoch check and the ref update (A02). A review's probes found them, not the suite.
findings.matters: These are the guarantees authorization, erasure and sync rest on. A bug here does not show as a failed turn; it shows as access that should have ended, or a write that should have been fenced.
findings.fix: A model-based test of each chain's reader against a reference, and multi-process interleavings of every fenced write path.
